Subject: Private deployment DPA — key custody & subprocessor alignment

Hi Elena / Acme procurement team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, I'm attaching a first-pass DPA focused on the private deployment option (VPC / on‑prem installer model) and the specific language Acme asked for around customer-controlled keys and operator access. High-level items in this draft: 

- BYOK/CMK responsibilities: customer holds the root CMK; Redwood operates compatible runtime images but should not retain unencrypted request payloads.
- Subprocessor list & notification: proposed 30-day notice for new subprocessors; explicit categories defined.
- Operator telemetry: hashes and aggregated metrics only; no raw payload capture allowed.
- Break-glass / emergency access: narrow, logged, and subject to legal hold.

Action items for you: please confirm whether Acme requires an escrow key arrangement, and whether you need an explicit keystore escrow SLA (e.g., access timeline, notarization). Also flag any other subprocessors we should pre-authorize.

Attachment: RI_DPA_privdep_draft_v1.pdf (DPA draft, 8 pages)

I'll leave Irene (security) and Naomi (legal) on copy for any technical/contract tweaks. Happy to hop on a short call to run through redlines.

Best,
Jordan Blake

Jordan — thanks for the draft. We reviewed with legal and clinical data security. A few immediate concerns: 

1) Subprocessor carveouts: the draft's subprocessor section is a bit broad. We need an explicit pre-approved list for any subprocessors that will process PHI-equivalent data (even if encrypted in transit) and a commitment that no new subprocessors will be used to process patient data without written consent.

2) Keystore/escrow: Acme's procurement policy requires either (a) customer-managed CMK with zero operator access, or (b) a documented escrow arrangement with a notary-backed retrieval process and a maximum retrieval SLA of 72 hours. Which model can Redwood support 1:1?

3) Evidence for operator telemetry: we need sample telemetry artifacts (fields and anonymization approach) before we can sign off.

We attached our redline for your team to review.

Attachment: Acme_DPA_redline_v1.docx (redline, comments inline)

Can we aim for a short call Thu morning BST?

Thanks,
Elena Ramos
Sr. Director, Information Risk — Acme Health

Elena — thanks for the quick review and the redline. A few clarifications and proposals below (quoting your points):

1) Subprocessors: Redwood's standard private-deploy stance is to provide a named-list for the initial release and commit to 30-day notice + written consent for any changes that would materially affect processing of regulated data. For PHI-equivalent workloads we can move to an explicit pre-approval requirement (we included a proposed table in the DPA where we list the infra subprocessors and the role). If Acme wants formal pre-approval for every infra subprocessor, we can add that clause but would need to manage operational cadence for updates.

2) Keystore/escrow: Redwood supports two operating modes: (A) Customer-held CMK in a cloud KMS or on-prem HSM where Redwood has zero ability to decrypt packet payloads; (B) Custodial escrow with notarized key escrow (we've implemented this for two customers — retrieval SLA options are 24/72/120 hours). If you require strict zero-operator decryption, choose (A); for an escrow model we can offer the 72-hour SLA with notarized handoff and auditable retrieval logs. Please indicate preference.

3) Operator telemetry: sample artifact: we propose that operator telemetry contains only: timestamp, service component identifier, hashed request id (SHA-256 salted), aggregate token counts, and high-level error codes. No payload, no identifiers that can be linked back to raw input. I'll ask Irene to provide a short sample schema and a short anonymization note.

Proposed next steps:
- Naomi and I can triage the redlines this afternoon and upload a consolidated draft to the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bRedwood-Acme-DPA
- If helpful, we can flip to a 30-minute call Thu 09:00 BST to walk procurement + legal through the two key options on keystore vs escrow.

Attachment: RI_DPA_privdep_draft_v1.pdf (updated to call out initial infra subprocessors)

Best,
Jordan

Hi Elena / team,

Thanks — quick technical points from security that we suggest adding to the DPA (internal rationale included):

- On-site audit window: we propose a mutually agreed 48-hour window for physical audits of on-prem deployments, with scoped objectives and an escort requirement. (Rationale: preserves Acme control while keeping audits efficient.)

- Subprocessor notification: 30 days notice for routine infra changes; immediate notification for any subprocessor changes that affect access to customer keys or telemetry. Add a narrow emergency exception that requires after-the-fact written notice within 24 hours and a full post-incident report within 14 days.

- Break-glass: define exact roles that can invoke break-glass (e.g., named Redwood SRE rotation + Acme-approved emergency contacts). Any invoked action must be recorded in an immutable audit log (timestamped) and Announced to Acme within 4 hours.

- Data residency confirmation: per our call we will ensure all storage and model artifact storage for this private deployment remains within the EU region unless Acme provides written consent for transfers. Please confirm the intended EU regions (e.g., eu-west-1, eu-central-1).

I'll coordinate a short artifact describing the operator telemetry schema and send that to the Drive folder today. Naomi — please advise on whether the escrow retrieval SLA wording needs a specific notarization vendor reference or if a generic notarization + audit evidence clause will suffice.

Irene Choi
Principal Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
